title.narrative: Capacity Development in Land Management Rwanda 2022-2027

description.narrative:
Programmet Capacity Development in Land Management in Rwanda, med aktivitetsperiod 2022-2027, är en fortsättning på pågående stöd till Lantmäteriet för myndighetens samarbete med och stöd till National Land Authority (NLA) i Rwanda (tidigare benämnt RLMUA). Den aktuella insatsen syftar till att bidra till att en transparent och pålitlig förvaltning av land, med möjlighet till ansvarutkrävande, driver en socio-ekonomisk transformation mot hållbar utveckling för alla i Rwanda.
De övergripande målen med insatsen är:
1. Projektstyrning: NLA ska vara en ledande och hållbar organisation för landförvaltning som koordinerar intressenter som bidrar till hållbar förvaltning av land för en socio-ekonomisk utveckling i Rwanda.
2. Landadministration: Att administration av land i Rwanda baseras på principer om transparens, effektivitet, jämställhet, jämlikhet, tillgång och ansvarsutkrävande och kan omhänderta sociala, legala och teknologiska förändringar för att leverera service till alla rwandier.
3. Lantmäteri, kartläggning och geografiskt informationssystem (GIS): Kompetent personal och hållbara system som ger korrekt, standardiserad och tillgänglig geo-spatial information, service och produkter som bidrar till socio-ekonomisk utveckling i Rwanda.
4. Landanvändningsplaner: Effektiv planering för landanvändning i Rwanda genom utveckling, genomförande, uppföljning och upplysning om Kigali stads- samt distriktsutvecklingsplaner, som är i linje med den nationella landanvändningsplanen för 2020-2050.

The programme Capacity Development in Land Management in Rwanda, with an activity period 2022-2027, is to a large extent a continuation of an ongoing support to the Swedish Mapping, Cadastre and Land Registration Authority (Lantmäteriet) for its collaboration and support to Rwanda National Land Authority (NLA). The programme will contribute to a transparent, reliable, and accountable land management is driving the socio-economic transformation towards a sustainable future for all Rwandans.
The expected outcomes of the intervention is
1. Project Management: NLA is a leading sustainable land management organization, driving coordination between key stakeholders contributing to sustainable socio-economic and environmental development for all Rwandans.
2. Land Administration: Land Administration in Rwanda is based on principles of transparency, efficiency, gender equality, accessibility and accountability and can accommodate social, legal and technological changes to deliver customer centred services to all Rwandans.
3. Surveying, Mapping and GIS: Capable staff and sustainable systems providing accurate, standardized and accessible geo-spatial information, services and products, contributing towards the socio-economic development in Rwanda.
4. Land Use Planning: Efficient land use management in Rwanda through development, implementation, monitoring and awareness of City of Kigali and Districts Land Use Master Plans, which are in compliance with the National Land Use and Development Master Plan 2020-2050 (NLUDMP).

The programme will contribute to that transparent, reliable, and accountable land management is driving the socio-economic transformation towards a sustainable future for all Rwandans.
The expected outcomes of the programme are:
Programme Management: NLA is a leading sustainable land management organization, driving coordination between key stakeholders contributing to sustainable management of land for socio-economic development for all Rwandans.
Land Administration: Land Administration in Rwanda is based on principles of transparency, efficiency, gender equality, equity, accessibility, and accountability and can accommodate social, legal and technological changes to deliver customer centered services to all Rwandans.

title.narrative: Capacity Building in Land Administration Rwanda Agreement 2022-2027
Capacity Building in Land Administration Rwanda Decision 2022-2027

description.narrative:
Project management. - Training on Results Based Measurement (RBM) was successfully conducted where 14 NLA staff participated in the training. The training targeted both the management staff and the project team. - The Registrar of land titles (Eastern Province) was supported by the project to participate in a land management training in Toulouse, France. The training concentrated on cadastre and taxation.
Land use planning - A four-day training workshop was conducted on holistic storm water management and environmental urban planning. the training also introduced the participants to Climate Fresk methodology a methodology which illustrates and clarifies causes and consequences of climate change. - Printed extracts of the DLUP map (the single layer land use plan) were provided at Cell level to assist in implementation and compliance with the land use plan and zoning regulations. - 13 awareness raising campaigns was conducted after the gazettement of approved DLUPs. This was supplemented with engagement with local governments, and largely through radios and TV campaigns. - 2day awareness and training session on DLUPs and land readjustment guidelines for detailed development plan elaboration was conducted with 55 district and provincial staff. - One (1) NLA staff was supported to attend the training at Erasmus University in Rotterdam, Netherlands.
GIS, Mapping and Surveying. - A surveying, GIS and Mapping strategic plan has been finalized. - Continued CORS maintenance field visits have been conducted. In May 2024 all 10 CORS stations were visited, focusing on general maintenance and cleaning of equipment and facilities. - Spider software was procured from Leica, with project funds. This software is crucial for better maintenance of Rwanda Geonet and the CORS network. Additionally, a training of NLA staff was performed to better familiarize them with the software. - a feasibility study for geoid implementation in Rwanda was finalized and it was conducted by a Swedish short expert Dr. Jonas Ågren. NLA is well-informed on the importance of introducing a uniform height system in Rwanda. - A comprehensive training for land surveyors and land administration district staff was carried out. The purpose of the training was to give participants training on different aspects of land administration, surveying and NSDI. - A pilot study of 3D mapping from KMZ/KML files was performed.
Land administration - Several trainings and awareness campaigns on new land law and land rights were conducted by both NLA and Haguruka. A total of 7091 persons and 520 local leaders were trained in districts of Nyanza, Bugesera and Rulindo - Training of 753 participants on land administration, service delivery, dispute resolution, surveying and land use management of. The participants included 31 NLA staff, 256 Private Land Surveyors and 466 District staff. - A pilot study was performed on informal transactions was conducted starting with 2 districts. This activity will continue into 2025. - Land clinics were organized and conducted in over 10 districts in connection to awareness campaigns. During these clinics, 500 land issues were received and resolved. - Boundary correction 1600 parcels boundaries were corrected. Additionally, communication materials for land disputes were designed and a framework with private land surveyors for boundary correction was elaborated and signed. - Design of Sales Price Register (SPR) is ongoing. Translation of SPR forms ongoing, development started in end of 2024. English and Kinyarwanda forms are done, French will be finished early 2025.
The key achievements in the annual report for 2025 include the following:
* Establishment and operationalization of an NLA Customer Care Center, including training-of-trainers, development of a strategic framework and procurement of a customer care telephone system.
* Significant progress in finalizing and improving District Land Use Plans (DLUPs), with 3 of the remaining 6 DLUPs approved and all including spatial SWOT analyses and district-specific strategies.
* Nationwide surveying inspections covering 296 private survey offices and official approval of the Cadastral Surveying Procedure Manual.
* Strengthened compliance and monitoring of Land use plans in 16 districts.
* Development and launch of LATIS (Land Administration Tracking Information System) to enhance transparency and monitoring of land administration processes.
* Awareness campaigns reaching more than 8,000 citizens directly and approximately 250,000 citizens via media.
* Demonstrated improvements in knowledge levels among training participants, including strong post-training score increases in land administration awareness activities.
Increased awareness and knowledge of land rights among citizens
During 2025 the project supported awareness campaigns in three districts (Rutsiro, Nyaruguru and Gakenke). The activities were performed with the partner Haguruka.
In total 606 local leaders (210 women and 396 men) were trained on land laws, land dispute resolution, inheritance, expropriation, and gender equality. Pre- and post-test evaluations in Rutsiro showed a 52.7% improvement in knowledge and skills, particularly among Executive Secretaries and Land Committee members. Over 85% of trained participants reported increased confidence in resolving disputes, advising citizens, and applying land laws more transparently and effectively.
Also, community outreach activities reached 8,049 citizens (3,976 women and 4,073 men). These sessions included addressing land registration, inheritance and succession, womens land rights, and peaceful dispute resolution, ensuring grassroots dissemination of essential information.
In addition to this the project supported NLA in conducting land clinics in each sector in the districts. This is a way of providing the authority service in remote places were people otherwise don't have access to NLA. The boundary corrections, made possible by project funding, help solving issues where parcel boundaries must be corrected. This helps solving or preventing land disputes among neighbours.
Better customer care delivery at NLA
Thanks to the project's support, NLA has greatly improved its ability to provide increased service to the public in 2025. At the end of the year, a customer care telephone system was implemented, it is said to be one of the first authorities in Rwanda to introduce such a system.
Prior to this, one of Lantmäteriet's experts has trained NLA staff in customer care during two missions and guided them in the development of a customer care strategy.
Currently, there is a team of about 8 people working as a call center group at NLA to provide answers to citizens' questions about land issues.
Inspection of private surveyors for better quality of cadastral surveying
During four weeks in March and April 2025, the project enabled NLA to conduct a field inspection of the country's private surveyors. The purpose was to investigate and evaluate their compliance with cadastral surveying instructions and standards.
In addition to compliance with regulations, the quality, standards of field data collected on ground by private surveyors were evaluated. NLA also checked the submission process of field data through IREMBO to LAIS from private surveyors and checked how private surveyors are filing physical file/archive for personal data security.
A total of 296 certified surveyors (out of 361) were inspected.
The inspection showed, among other things, that 204 certified surveyors are complying with cadastral surveying instructions. 39 certified surveyors were found with malpractices subject to being suspended.
3 certified surveyors were found with conflict of interest to be suspended. 49 certified surveyors found missing some requirements and asked to provide an explanation.
The inspections will continue and will contribute to increased compliance with cadastral regulations and standards. This in turn will lead to increased quality of cadastral data in Rwanda.
Tackling informal land transactions in Rwanda
What is the reason behind the continued existence of informal land transactions in Rwanda? With the support of the project (financial and expert support), NLA has attempted to answer this question through a large survey conducted in five districts in late 2024 and early 2025. A total of 1,533 people who had carried out land transactions were interviewed. In summary, the survey concluded that the top cause of informality is neither the cost nor the process. This indicates that the efforts of NLA to reduce costs and simplify processes are fruitful. The top cause of informality according to the study is reluctant sellers or sellers lacking registration in the first place.
Thanks to this survey, there is now an up-to-date picture of the situation, allowing the NLA to move forward and develop a strategy to counter informal land transactions. This is important from several aspects, not least for landowners to be able to truly assert the legal right to the land they own. In addition to legal certainty, it is important to have a property register that has accurate and up-to-date information about who owns the country's properties.
